test: Value each scrap report (dimension out of tolerance + operator error, and all reasons) at the SO line PO unit price x quantity. Rank parts (part_id), families, op/work-centre combos, and employees (via labour qty_scrap) by scrap value; compute the share carried by the top 10% of each population (among those with any volume, not only those with scrap). Normalise by volume: scrap pieces per piece run/ordered per part and per employee, compare dispersion to a binomial/Poisson expectation. Check persistence: overlap of top-decile parts between years, and year-to-year correlation of per-entity scrap rate. Also check first-run vs repeat jobs and new hires vs tenured.
support: Top 10% of parts or op/work-centre combos carry >50% of scrap value, AND scrap rate per piece varies well beyond what volume/chance explains, AND the same entities stay on top across years (or first runs/new hires show materially higher rates).
weaken: Top-decile share mostly mirrors share of volume/value shipped (Pareto follows volume); per-piece rates roughly uniform; top lists change randomly year to year.
expect: Moderate confidence that a value Pareto will show top 10% of parts >50% of scrap value, because part value and volume are themselves highly skewed. I expect much of that to follow volume/price, with per-piece rate concentration weaker; work-centre view will be dominated by where scrap is found (laser/brake/inspect). Employee concentration likely mostly follows hours worked. Maybe 60% that the volume-normalised concentration is weak.
